pages.title: A – C
pages.body:
- **Alternate angles:** Equal angles on opposite sides of a transversal, between two parallel lines (Z-shape).
- **Angle of depression:** The angle below the horizontal at which an observer looks down at an object.
- **Angle of elevation:** The angle above the horizontal at which an observer looks up at an object.
- **Binomial:** An algebraic expression with two terms, e.g. x + 3.
- **Co-interior angles:** Angles on the same side of a transversal between parallel lines; they add up to 180°.
- **Constant of proportionality:** The constant k in y = kx; the unit rate of a proportional relationship.
- **Continuous data:** Data obtained by measuring, which can take any value in a range.
- **Corresponding angles:** Equal angles in matching positions where a transversal crosses parallel lines (F-shape).
- **Cosine:** In a right-angled triangle, cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse.

pages.title: D – L
pages.body:
- **Discrete data:** Data obtained by counting, taking separate (usually whole-number) values.
- **Exponential equation:** An equation in which the unknown is in the index, e.g. 2ˣ = 16.
- **Factorise:** To write an expression as a product of its factors.
- **Gradient:** The steepness of a line: change in y ÷ change in x.
- **Hypotenuse:** The longest side of a right-angled triangle, opposite the right angle.
- **Independent events:** Events where the outcome of one does not affect the outcome of the other.
- **Inequality:** A statement using <, >, ≤ or ≥ to compare two quantities.
- **Intersection (of sets):** The set of elements common to both sets, A ∩ B.
- **Laws of indices:** Rules for simplifying powers, e.g. aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ.

pages.title: L – S
pages.body:
- **Locus:** The set of all points that satisfy a given condition.
- **Mode:** The value that occurs most often in a set of data.
- **Ordinal data:** Non-numeric data that can be put in order, e.g. grades.
- **Perfect square:** A number that is the square of a whole number, e.g. 49 = 7².
- **Proportional:** Two quantities whose ratio is always the same; their graph is a straight line through the origin.
- **Pythagoras' theorem:** In a right-angled triangle, a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse.
- **Range:** The difference between the largest and smallest values in a set of data.
- **Rotation:** A transformation that turns a shape about a fixed centre through a given angle.
- **Sine:** In a right-angled triangle, sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse.

pages.title: S – Y
pages.body:
- **Standard form:** A number written as A × 10ⁿ where 1 ≤ A < 10 and n is an integer.
- **Stem-and-leaf plot:** A display that splits each value into a stem and a leaf and lists leaves in order.
- **Tangent (ratio):** In a right-angled triangle, tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent.
- **Transversal:** A line that crosses two or more other lines.
- **Tree diagram:** A diagram of branches showing the outcomes and probabilities of successive events.
- **Union (of sets):** The set of all elements in either set, A ∪ B.
- **Unit rate:** A rate for one unit of the second quantity.
- **Waffle diagram:** A 10 × 10 grid in which each cell represents 1%.
- **y-intercept:** The point where a line crosses the y-axis; c in y = mx + c.
